content:
The test image shows two bell pepper fruits with large, dark (black/brown), sunken necrotic lesions covering most of the fruit surface. There's a concentric ring-like pattern in the lesions. This is classic fruit rot.

Top candidates: Anthracnose (sunken dark circular lesions on fruit), Phytophthora_Blight (dark water-soaked fruit lesions), Late_Blight, and Alternaria_Black_Molds_Stem_Cankers.

Now viewing one reference from each of my top 4 candidates:

Key observations from the test image:
- Two bell peppers with massive dark (black/brown), sunken, water-soaked lesions covering most of the fruit surface
- Bugwood ID **1568070** in the test image; the Phytophthora_Blight reference (Bugwood_100.jpg) has ID **1568066** — consecutive IDs from the same photographer/disease documentation series
- The Anthracnose reference (Bugwood_13, ID 5549819) shows a much smaller, more defined circular lesion — inconsistent with the large fruit rot in the test

The large, dark, water-soaked fruit rot covering most of the pepper surface, combined with the consecutive Bugwood IDs matching the Phytophthora_Blight reference series, strongly points to Phytophthora_Blight (caused by *Phytophthora capsici* on pepper).
